- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values by 1–2%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to compensate for bearish bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward revisions to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model lags in adjusting; shift forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per day of lag.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is > 82, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until price stabilizes.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
